Phosphocreatine is synthesized in the mitochondria by the enzyme creatine kinase (mitochondrial isoform), but it is stored and utilized primarily in the cytoplasm, particularly in the sarcoplasm of muscle cells, where it serves as a rapid reservoir for regenerating ATP during high-intensity activity.  
It is not found in all subcellular compartments, nor is it located in the sarcolemma.  
Thus, the main storage site relevant to the question is the cytoplasm.
